subject: [PATCH] mm/vmscan: reclaim every zone in per-node proactive reclaim

reviews.author: Balbir Singh
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the code has unrelated issues and will be sending separate patches to address them.
reviews.raw_body:
I just noticed some other issues with this code, in terms of honouring
zone_reclaim_node (not related to this patch). I'll send out fixes, for
this patch.

Reviewed-by: Balbir Singh <balbirs@nvidia.com>

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Michal Hocko suggested changing the gfp_mask from GFP_KERNEL to GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE in user_proactive_reclaim() to fix an issue with try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages.

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary: reviewer noted that proactive reclaim isn't serving an allocation, so capping the scan to ZONE_NORMAL is unnecessary and suggested using MAX_NR_ZONES - 1 or GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE instead
reviews.raw_body:
reclaim_idx = MAX_NR_ZONES - 1 is the right fix \u2014 proactive reclaim
isn't serving an allocation, so gfp_zone(GFP_KERNEL) needlessly caps
the scan.  GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE would also work for the node path
via gfp_zone(), but that's indirect.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <chentao@kylinos.cn>

reviews.author: Davidlohr Bueso
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch makes sense and is glad people are using the proactive reclaim interface, explicitly giving an Acked-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
This makes sense - sorry for the trouble but at least glad to see
people using this interface.

Acked-by: Davidlohr Bueso <dave@stgolabs.net>

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages already scans all zones, but disagreed on whether the gfp_mask should be GFP_KERNEL.
reviews.raw_body:
funny enough, try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages does what my patch does:

struct scan_control sc = {
	.reclaim_idx = MAX_NR_ZONES - 1,


now, whether the gfp_mask should be GFP_KERNEL, that's a different
question i think.

(tl;dr i think my patch is still correct)

~Gregory

-- 
Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that tweaking the gfp_mask to reclaim all zones is more consistent, but left the decision up to the author.
reviews.raw_body:
Ohh, right, I forgot that memcg reclaim always reclaims all zones.
Tweaking the mask seems more consistent but not something I will insist
on. Up to you which way to go. In any case

Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch modifies the per-node proactive reclaim function to scan every zone, not just ZONE_NORMAL, in order to reclaim movable memory as well. This addresses a problem where nodes with only movable memory were not being reclaimed properly. The approach taken is to change the `reclaim_idx` field of the `scan_control` structure to always set it to the maximum number of zones, allowing all zones to be scanned.

reviews.author: SJ Park
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch does not address the issue of reclaiming movable memory, which is skipped due to the gfp_zone(GFP_KERNEL) limit in user_proactive_reclaim(), and requested that every zone be scanned as per the original proactive reclaim interface.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that their interface has bugs and is surprised by reviewer's feedback, but does not commit to fixing them.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm shocked, I tell you, shocked!

These are all things I accidentally ran into by just uh... using the
interface.  I'm absolutely positive these interfaces are full of bugs.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Balbir Singh
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch's proactive reclaim may violate the contract for cgroups reclaim interface by setting .may_writepage and .may_unmap to 1, which could conflict with node zone reclaim constraints.
sentiment_signals: violation of default node reclaim parameters
reviews.raw_body:
:)

I was looking at making may_writepage and may_unmap align with the
constraints of node zone reclaim, .may_writepage = !!(node_reclaim_mode & RECLAIM_WRITE),
and .may_unmap = !!(node_reclaim_mode & RECLAIM_UNMAP), which may
violate the contract for proactive reclaim. Proactive reclaim itself
tries to be compatible with cgroups reclaim interface, so it sets these
values to 1. I still feel it is a violation of default node reclaim
parameters, but not sure if it needs to be fixed up.

Balbir
